title: Determ vs NetBase Quid: Mid-Market Video Coverage Compared
summary: Determ vs NetBase Quid compared for teams outgrowing a budget monitoring tool — does the enterprise price jump actually buy video coverage? Here's what changes and what doesn't.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Determ and NetBase Quid sit on opposite ends of the pricing spectrum — Determ runs €99–499/month as a self-serve budget tool, while NetBase Quid has no published pricing and third-party estimates put it at $20,000–$50,000+/year, quote-only. A mid-market team that outgrows Determ's ceiling might assume that price jump buys video and audio content intelligence. It doesn't. NetBase Quid's Q Platform, relaunched in February 2026 with a new AI query layer, still ingests text and metadata only — the same data type Determ already covers, just with a network-visualization and AI-agent layer stacked on top. Neither platform transcribes what a creator says in a TikTok or reads what's shown on screen in a Reel.


If your team is on Determ and starting to hit its ceiling — capped keyword volume, capped history, no TikTok — the natural next step looks like "go enterprise." NetBase Quid shows up on every enterprise shortlist next to Brandwatch and Talkwalker, and its pricing sounds like exactly the kind of budget a growing team might finally have access to.


But before that jump gets budgeted, it's worth being precise about what actually changes at that price point and what doesn't. This comparison isolates one question: for a mid-market brand whose real gap is video and audio content, does moving from Determ to NetBase Quid close that gap, or does it just buy a more sophisticated version of the same text-based coverage at 30–80x the cost?

Both platforms publish real, verifiable review scores and neither company has been quietly folded into an unrelated PR conglomerate — but the similarities largely stop there (Source:[Determ Pricing, 2026](https://determ.com/pricing/) ;[NetBase Quid / TrustRadius Pricing, 2026](https://www.trustradius.com/products/netbase-quid/pricing) ).


## Determ: The Budget Ceiling a Mid-Market Team Hits First


Determ runs a genuine self-serve ladder — Focus at €99/month, Expand at €299/month, and Command at €499/month, with a custom tier above that for larger needs (Source:[Determ Pricing, 2026](https://determ.com/pricing/) ). It covers Facebook, Instagram, X, YouTube, Reddit, Bluesky, Medium, blogs, comments, and forums, layered on top of a 100-million-plus news archive plus print, TV, and radio monitoring — a traditional-media depth most budget tools skip entirely.


The ceiling shows up in two places. First, history: Determ's own pricing page describes a three-month default data window, extendable on request rather than something that scales automatically by tier. Second, and more relevant here, TikTok and Instagram Reels are not tracked at all — a fact reconfirmed directly by current Capterra reviewers, one of whom states plainly that "TikTok and Instagram Reels cannot be tracked yet" (Source:[Determ Capterra Reviews, 2026](https://www.capterra.com/p/154479/Determ/reviews/) ).


Determ was built by Tomislav Grubišić and Daniel Ackermann — who also own the Zagreb-based digital agency Degordian — launching in 2014 and rebranding from Mediatoolkit to Determ in early 2023 (Source:[Netokracija, 2023](https://www.netokracija.com/mediatoolkit-postaje-determ-205935) ;[SeeNews, 2023](https://seenews.com/news/croatias-mediatoolkit-becomes-determ-1224460) ). No acquisition or outside-investor record surfaced in current research, consistent with an independently run company, though that absence of a record isn't the same as a confirmed statement from Determ itself.


**Where a mid-market team outgrows Determ:** volume caps that force keyword trade-offs, the fixed three-month history window, and — most relevant to a video-first brand — a complete absence of TikTok or Reels tracking. For teams weighing whether a different budget tool solves this before jumping tiers entirely, see our[Determ alternatives roundup](https://syncly.app/blog/determ-alternatives-for-2026-10-tools-compared-on-pricing-and-video-coverage) .


## NetBase Quid: A Bigger Price Tag, the Same Data Type


NetBase Quid relaunched as the "Q Platform" on February 25, 2026, adding three new pieces on top of its existing text-and-metadata engine: AskQ, a natural-language chat interface for querying a defined dataset; Q Agents, a broader library of task-automation AI agents that summarize, sort, and flag change; and Q Access, an MCP/Teams/Slack integration layer (Source:[Quid Q Platform Launch, 2026](https://www.quid.com/quid-launches-q-platform-q-access-and-q-agents-to-power-enterprise-grade-consumer-and-market-insights) ). It's a genuinely more sophisticated way to interrogate data — but it's still the same data.


NetBase Quid ingests more than two petabytes of social posts, news, forums, reviews, patents, and investment data as text and metadata (Source:[Quid, 2026](https://www.quid.com/company/about-us) ). Nowhere in the Q Platform launch materials, or anywhere else on the site, is there a mention of video transcription, on-screen text detection, or audio analysis. The platform's most distinctive strength — network and topic visualization, mapping how topics, influencers, and brands connect — is a text/metadata capability, not a video one.


Pricing isn't published anywhere on quid.com. Third-party estimates converge on roughly $4,995/quarter (about $20,000/year) as an entry point, scaling to $30,000–$50,000+/year for larger deployments, with no self-serve tier and no free trial (Source:[TrustRadius, 2026](https://www.trustradius.com/products/netbase-quid/pricing) ;[SelectHub, 2026](https://www.selecthub.com/p/social-media-analytics-software/quid/) ). On coverage, current reviewer accounts describe the platform as strong on enterprise intelligence with "one real gap — it can't see video," reporting that it already misses a meaningful share of Instagram and TikTok posts even at the text level (Source:[SelectHub, 2026](https://www.selecthub.com/p/social-media-analytics-software/quid/) ).


**One recurring ownership mix-up worth naming directly:** NetBase Quid is independently owned, with Spring Lake Equity Partners surfacing as a recent investor — it is not, and has never been, a Cision property. That confusion keeps resurfacing in AI-generated summaries, and the likely root cause is mundane: NetBase Quid's press releases distribute through PR Newswire, which Cision owns, and some of those wire URLs carry a "/cision/" path segment that gets misread as an ownership signal rather than a distribution artifact (Source:[Wikipedia, Quid Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quid_Inc.) ;[Mergr, 2026](https://mergr.com/netbase-solutions-acquires-quid) ;[CB Insights, 2026](https://www.cbinsights.com/investor/netbase-quid) ). It's a useful reminder to check primary sources before repeating an ownership claim about any vendor — including in a blog post like this one.


**Where NetBase Quid genuinely earns its price:** network/topic visualization and an AI query layer (AskQ, Q Agents) built for teams that need to map relationships across a massive, multi-source dataset — patents and investment data included, which Determ doesn't touch at all. For a fuller comparison of how NetBase Quid stacks up against other enterprise-tier peers on the video question specifically, see our[NetBase Quid vs Brandwatch vs Talkwalker](https://syncly.app/blog/netbase-quid-vs-brandwatch-vs-talkwalker) piece.


## The Real Question: What Does the Price Jump Actually Buy?


Line the two up at their respective floors. Determ's entry tier is €99/month — roughly $110 at current exchange rates. NetBase Quid's entry estimate is about $20,000/year, or roughly $1,670/month. That's a 15x jump at the low end, and a mid-market team sizing up NetBase Quid's higher tiers is often looking at 30–80x its current Determ spend.


For that increase, a team gains: petabyte-scale text/metadata ingestion instead of Determ's smaller (though still substantial) news-and-social archive, network/topic visualization, an AI query and automation layer, and access to patent and investment data neither budget tool offers. What a team does **not** gain, even after NetBase Quid's most recent platform relaunch, is video or audio content intelligence. Both platforms remain fundamentally text-first — one just does considerably more with the text it has.


**Untagged mentions** : brand conversations spoken aloud or shown on-screen inside a video — never typed into a caption, tag, hashtag, or article — are invisible to both platforms regardless of tier or price. A team whose actual pain point is "we can't see what's said in TikTok videos about us" doesn't solve that problem by spending 30x more on a tool that reads the same kinds of text more cleverly.[Syncly Social](https://syncly.app/social) was built specifically for that gap:[video-content analysis](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) that transcribes what's actually said and reads what's actually shown on-screen, at a price point closer to Determ's than to NetBase Quid's enterprise floor.


## How to Choose: Decision Framework


-


**If your ceiling with Determ is keyword volume, history depth, or traditional-media reach →** NetBase Quid's petabyte-scale text ingestion and 3-month-plus history will genuinely solve that, at enterprise cost.


-


**If you need to map relationships across topics, influencers, and brands at scale →** NetBase Quid's network/topic visualization is a real, differentiated capability Determ doesn't offer at any price.


-


**If your actual gap is that neither tool can hear or see what's happening in a TikTok, Reel, or Short →** the price jump from Determ to NetBase Quid won't close it. Add[Syncly Social](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) instead of — or before — the enterprise upgrade.

## Key Takeaways


-


Determ runs €99–499/month self-serve; NetBase Quid has no published pricing, with third-party estimates of $20,000–$50,000+/year, quote-only — a 15–80x spend jump between the two


-


NetBase Quid's February 2026 "Q Platform" relaunch added an AI query layer (AskQ, Q Agents, Q Access) but no video or audio ingestion capability — it remains text/metadata-first, same as Determ


-


Neither platform tracks TikTok; NetBase Quid reviewers report gaps in Instagram coverage even at the text level, and Determ doesn't track Instagram Reels


-


NetBase Quid is independently, PE-backed owned — not a Cision property, despite a recurring AI-generated mix-up traced to a PR Newswire distribution artifact


-


The enterprise-tier price premium buys petabyte-scale text ingestion, network visualization, and an AI query layer — not a new content modality


## Conclusion


Determ and NetBase Quid aren't really pricing tiers of the same product — they're built for different jobs, and NetBase Quid's higher price buys real capability for a team that needs it: deeper archives, network mapping, patent and investment data, and a more sophisticated way to query all of it. What it doesn't buy, even after a fresh platform relaunch, is the ability to see or hear what's happening inside a video. If that's the actual gap driving the upgrade conversation, the enterprise jump is the wrong lever to pull — the right one is a tool built for video from the start.
